parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student: • closes the switch • records the voltmeter reading V • records the ammeter reading I • opens the switch. Fig. 2.2 shows the readings on the voltmeter and the ammeter. Record the readings on the voltmeter and the ammeter in the first row of Table 2.1. Fig. 2.2 Table 2.1 resistance between X and Y / Ω V / V I / A R / Ω 10 13 0.83 0.27 20 0.81 4.5 [2]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Calculate the resistance R of the diode using your meter readings from (a) . Use the equation R = V I . Record your answer in the first row of Table 2.1 to an appropriate number of significant figures. [2]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student: • connects a 3 Ω resistor in series with the 10 Ω resistor between terminals X and Y, as shown in Fig. 2.3, and repeats the procedure in (a) Fig. 2.3 • connects the 7 Ω , 10 Ω and 3 Ω resistors in series between X and Y, as shown in Fig. 2.4, and repeats the procedure in (a) . parts.text: (d) As the resistance between terminals X and Y is increased, the current in the circuit changes. Use your results in Table 2.1 to state the relationship between the current in the circuit and:
